metadata.case_name: WONG HAK MAN v. HARVEST ENGINEERING DEVELOPMENT LIMITED AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: A thin dense area over the left frontal lobe (subdural haematoma).
source: A Computerized Tomography scan revealed a thin dense area over the left frontal lobe. This subdural haematoma was conservatively treated and a further CT scan on the following day was normal.

injuries.description: Abrasions over the left side of his neck, abdominal wall, left elbow, right thigh and right ankle.
injuries.body_part: left side of neck; abdominal wall; left elbow; right thigh; right ankle
source: Examination revealed that he had suffered abrasions over the left side of his neck, abdominal wall, left elbow, right thigh and right ankle.

injuries.description: Fractured talus in the right ankle.
source: X-ray disclosed a fractured talus in the right ankle.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

injuries.description: Some hearing loss of a mild grade in both ears and tinnitus.
source: Two Ear, Nose & Throat experts, Drs. Lo Siu Sing and Henri KL Chu jointly examined him, diagnosing that he had suffered some hearing loss of a mild grade in both ears and tinnitus as a highly probable result of the accident.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of middle or inner ear

source: I also find that as a result of the accident, the Plaintiff has suffered post concussional syndrome and depressive episode of a mild to moderate nature.
I also find that as a result of the accident, the Plaintiff has suffered post concussional syndrome and depressive episode of a mild to moderate nature.

manifestations.description: Persistent headaches, sometimes debilitating and lasting for hours.
Mild hearing loss in both ears.
Swelling and tenderness over the right ankle.
Reduced range of movement of the right ankle joint (about half of left side).
Residual aches and pains and some stiffness in the ankle.
Moderate global impairment in higher mental function (as described by an expert).
Depressive symptoms (depressive episode): low motivation, fatigue, anxiety, distress and absenteeism.
Needed a walking stick at time of assessment; difficulty squatting and unsteady standing.

treatments_received: Open reduction and screw fixation of the ankle (27 November 2003)
Physiotherapy (16 sessions spanning January to May 2004)
Conservative treatment for subdural haematoma (CT scan and observation)
Admission to Tuen Mun Hospital and transfer to orthopaedic ward (19 November 2003)
Admission to Pok Oi Hospital for physiotherapy and rehabilitation (3 December 2003 to 6 January 2004)
treatments_future: Psychiatric treatment recommended: 20 sessions of psychotherapy with medication at fortnightly intervals (course about 10 months)

losses.description: Residual stiffness, minor aches and pain and tenderness in the right ankle following talar fracture.
At assessment required walking stick, could only squat half-way and was unsteady standing on either foot or walking on toes or heels (reduced mobility demonstrated at assessment).
A small degree of bilateral hearing impairment and tinnitus.
Tender scar noted at right ankle.
Poor memory and cognitive difficulties associated with post concussional syndrome and depressive episode.
